name: Cua
tagline: Open-source infrastructure for computer-use agents across full desktops.
description: Cua (also styled c/ua) is infrastructure for building and scaling computer-use agents. One API boots Linux, Windows, macOS, and Android machines in lightweight, isolated virtual containers, and SDKs plus benchmarks let agents observe and control full operating systems — clicking, typing, browsing, and running real apps. On Apple Silicon it reaches near-native speed via Apple's Virtualization.framework and the Lume CLI, and it runs locally with any LLM or on Cua's managed cloud.
insight: A Y Combinator X25 company; its MIT-licensed core crossed 15k GitHub stars.

modelSupport.notes: Run locally or in the cloud with any LLM you choose.

edge: Boots Linux/Windows/macOS/Android VMs from one API for computer-use agents, hitting near-native speed on Apple Silicon via Apple's Virtualization.framework.
pros: Isolated VMs across four OS families
Agents control full desktops, not just browsers
cons: Developer/infra tool, not an end-user app
